notes: Intro: Bryxton Residency AI is an enterprise insurance platform processing PHI-adjacent claims data; evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for inference of policy & claims workflows.
Decision drivers: strict EU data residency, customer-managed KMS, audit trail for model inputs/outputs, ability to run private control plane with limited outbound-only connectivity.
Primary workload: claims-automation (NLP summarization + policy extraction) + agent assist for contact center. Peak: 120 concurrent chat sessions, steady-state embeddings workload ~50k/day.
Latency/throughput targets: p95 text-generation latency <200ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens); batching acceptable for bulk embedding jobs; throughput requirement ~800 reqs/min at peak.

Model preferences: prefer open/quantized models (MPT/Llama-derivatives) with customer option to pin model versions. Require deterministic fallback policy to smaller quantized model if capacity constrained.
Security review status: initial security questionnaire (shared 2026-02-20) received; SSO/SAML & SCIM required. SOC2 & ISO27001 certificates requested — provided by Redwood (pending legal review).

KMS/Encryption: MUST support customer-managed CMKs in AWS (BYOK). Requirement: no plaintext keys leave customer account; key usage logs should appear in their CloudTrail. Need KMS integration runbook for key rotation and key policy sample.

Data residency / storage: all inference and embeddings must remain in eu-west-1. No cross-region replication without express approval from Bryxton security/legal. Also require configurable retention rules (30/90/365 days) for logs and KV caches.

Audit logging: full request/response metadata (token counts, model id, timestamps) exported to customer CloudWatch/CloudTrail or via syslog to their Splunk. Customer wants verified SLA for log delivery latency (<5 min).

Network/architecture constraints: design asked for dedicated VPC per customer with two private subnets across two AZs, NAT gateway for egress-only, no inbound public IPs. Preferred connectivity: AWS PrivateLink or Transit Gateway to Bryxton corporate VPC. Control plane calls must be outbound-only to pinned Redwood control endpoints.

Inbound/outbound notes: inbound from internet blocked. Inbound access for admin console via SSO from Bryxton corporate SAML IdP over PrivateLink. Outbound only to specific IP ranges/domains; listed egress endpoints must be documented for firewall rules.

Regions & failover: primary eu-west-1; DR plans to eu-central-1 but only after legal approval for replication. Bryxton requires RTO/RPO targets for model serving (RTO 15m, RPO minimal for request logs).

Operational hooks: must provide token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, and alerting for model quality regressions tied to a fixed prompt set. Bryxton wants a short onboarding checklist for day-0 (certs, KMS, VPC peering, test prompts).

POC scope: 4-week POC to demonstrate (1) VPC topology + PrivateLink connectivity, (2) CMK-backed storage for model caches, (3) audit log export to Splunk, (4) p95 latency benchmarks with pinned quantized model. Success criteria defined in drive doc.
